hypotheses: Real, not as filed: the income yield exceeds the published holdings rate by 3.8 to 7.0 points because on about 100 floating loans per quarter the published interest_rate is the FLOOR of the printed formula ('Prime + 4.0 % or Floor rate 11.5 %' publishes 11.5). The shared identifier-text reader (pipeline/staging_bdc.py, _text_interest_rate) reads 'Floor rate' as the rate on purpose.

Fix options, each an owner decision with about 1,450 rows over 14 quarters: (a) withdraw the floor (rate null, spread and reference kept; the fund then joins f27-wac-from-fixed-rate-rows-only-floating-coupons-not-printed), by a wrapper-gated switch in the text reader (shared code) or by row corrections; (b) compute max(reference on the date + spread, floor) as a labelled derived rate, which the convention does not cover today.
Not done here: the change moves a published figure on half the loan book and the convention for a formula-only filer is not settled.
One context for two printed lines; would need a row-add path that accepts a second row with the same identifier, or a context_identifiers-style setting that clones a context.
